The Herald of 7 May 2010 carried the Honors College's own full-page congratulations advertisement, and its Honors Program Graduates column lists 'Hannah Pennington, Biochemistry' among the May 2010 graduates. A Hannah Pennington therefore took her WKU degree in May 2010, which is exactly what a student sworn to the Student Senate in September 2008 would do, and it is not what the woman in WKU's 'Hannah Pennington Spotlight' of 25 January 2022 did: that article's subject came through the Gatton Academy, graduated in 2015 with the Mahurin Honors College CE/T of the Year and started medical school that autumn. Two different women. Do not publish wku.edu/img_news/article_images/10188.jpg. The 2010 advertisement is a name list and carries no photographs, so it gives a date and not a face.

name: DEFECTIVE SCAN: 2015 Talisman, printed pages 268-313
fact: TopSCHOLAR's scan of the 2015 Talisman: Resurgence (dlsc_ua_records/8679) is missing its entire student PORTRAITS section. The folios run continuously to 267 on PDF page 138 and resume at 314-315 on PDF page 140, with one uncaptioned full-bleed image between them; no page in the file carries a folio between 268 and 313. The book's own back index, which IS in the file, indexes people to those pages, so they exist in print: 'Scaff, Tyler 290', 'Smith, Sherry 291', 'Spalding, Shelley 292', 'Wilkins, Hayley 295', 'Havel, Catherine 279'. Tyler Scaff, the Campus Improvements chair of 2013-14 and 2014-15, therefore has a printed portrait at p. 290 that cannot be reached through TopSCHOLAR. There is no Part II: records 8677 and 8678 are the two 2016 issues and 8676 and 8680 are unrelated collections. If a complete copy of this volume ever surfaces, page 290 is the single highest-value page in it for this archive.

name: SOURCE NOTE: the 2015 Talisman club pages
fact: The club and organisation spread of the 2015 Talisman, printed pp. 316-333, is worth knowing about because it is half usable and half not. Some groups are keyed positionally, 'Row 1: ... The large groups, chiefly the sororities and the honour societies, are captioned with a single alphabetical list and no positions at all, and a grid of faces against an alphabetical list identifies nobody. Checked and refused on that ground: Megan Skaggs on p. 323, Sarah Hazelip and Ashley Presnell on p. 329, Alexis Baker and Hayley Wilkins and Catherine Havel on p. 316, Brenna Duncan and Alyson Manley on p. 327, Catherine Havel and Alyson Manley again on p. 331. Do not cut faces from those.

name: SOURCE FOUND: the 2016 Talisman is the portrait book this block needed
fact: dlsc_ua_records/8677, '2016 Talisman - Life More Life', 755,645,090 bytes and 180 pages, is the only volume in this era with a COMPLETE portrait section, and it produced six of this run's nine finds. It carries seniors on printed pp. 234-257, underclassmen on 258-295, graduate students on 296-299 and faculty and staff on 300-305, plus a full back index on 344-352 that lists every person in the book with page numbers. Grep the index first. The layout is the same throughout: a grid of square studio portraits, three or four to a row, with that row's names set in the outer margin in ONE COLUMN, top to bottom against left to right, and the names running alphabetically down the page. Verify the pairing on the same spread by counting the sexes in a neighbouring row before cutting anything; on p. 253 there is an even better check, because the third portrait of the second row wears a t-shirt printed GEOLOGY and the margin prints GEOLOGY under Paul Shively's name. Do not overlook the faculty and staff grid when hunting students: former officers who took university jobs are in it, which is where Elizabeth McGrew and Catherine Havel were found.

name: Tyler Scaff
fact: CONFIRMED AND LEFT. The 2015 Talisman's own back index reads 'Scaff, Tyler 290'. Printed page 290 sits inside the student portraits section, printed pp. 268-313, which is absent from TopSCHOLAR's scan of the volume: the copy on disk runs 266-267 on PDF page 138, carries an uncredited full-bleed photograph with no folio on PDF page 139, and resumes at 'PORTRAITS - FACULTY & STAFF 315 / 314' on PDF page 140. The faculty-and-staff spread that does survive holds 21 names and Scaff is not among them, as expected for a student. The index itself, PDF pp. 156-159, is complete and was read line by line: of the 31 officers only Scaff is indexed into the missing range. Page 290 exists in print and in no copy we can reach. Verified independently against the 2016 Talisman, whose grids and 3,190-line index contain no Tyler Scaff at all, so the 2015 portrait is the only one. Confirmed 7 September 2026; leave it.

name: Sarah Hazelip
fact: FOUND IN THE 2015 TALISMAN AND NOT USABLE. name: SOURCE CLOSURE - all 31 officers of _officers-n0813.json
fact: THE HERALD PRINT CAPTION INDEX, READ WITH ITS 'ABOVE' FIELD, IS NOW TESTED AGAINST THIS BLOCK AND HOLDS NONE OF IT. Both indexes were swept: _herald-index-2002-2009/photo_captions_above_2002-2009.jsonl and all eleven files of _herald-index-2010-2016/, which now reaches 2019. Every photograph's text BELOW, RIGHT OF and ABOVE the frame was matched against all 31 officers on first-name-plus-surname with initial and nickname variants. Forty-two hits came back and every one was read by hand; not one is a photograph of one of these officers. The near misses worth recording: the SGA election-results page of 8 April 2011 (dlsc_ua_records/6616, p. 3) prints Mac Mullins, David Spalding, Rachel Calhoun, Eileen Forsythe and Brittany Crowley in its list of winning STUDENT SENATORS, but the page carries only two portraits and both belong to the executive winners, Kendrick Bryan and Devon Hilderbrandt; the graduation advertisement of 4 May 2012 (6557, p. 11) sets 'David W. Spalding' in a Political Science graduate list beside a decorative image, not a portrait; Cole McDowell is named in the lead story of 20 November 2014 (6399, p. 1) and the two photographs on that page are of Shantytown; Tyler Scaff is named in senate reports of 14 November 2013 (6379), 13 February 2014 (6519) and 1 May 2014 (6499) and none of those pages photographs him. Three further passes were run to catch what a full-name match cannot: a mugshot-nameplate pass over every image between 40 and 600 px wide whose caption is under 70 characters and carries an officer surname (13 hits, all other people - Nick Simmons, Todd Stewart, Kwabena Boateng of Fort Mitchell, Meaghan Howell, Shayna Crowley); a harvest-then-match pass over all 237 photographs in 2002-2019 whose caption mentions SGA, student government, the student senate or the judicial council, matched on surname alone (one hit, senator Wes Calhoun of Indianapolis, 3 February 2009, not Rachel Calhoun); and a full-text pass for context. One coverage gap is worth recording for a later run: the 2002-2009 caption index has no records for September 2008 or December 2008, and none for August-December 2006.

name: Chris Jankowski
fact: REFUSAL RE-TESTED AND UPHELD. _do-not-use.json refuses the Herald photograph of 7 December 2010, resident assistants making signs in Pearce-Ford Tower, on the ground that the caption names three people and nothing separates the two men. The frame was opened and counted this run: three people are in it, one woman kneeling at the left, one man bent over painting in the centre and one man seated at the right edge. The caption names Laqisha Walton and 'Versailles sophomore Chris Jankowski' as the two resident assistants making signs and then quotes 'Nicholasville junior Matt Brockman', giving no positions for any of them. Walton is identifiable as the only woman; the two men are not separable. The refusal is correct and stands. This is the only frame in the whole 21,304-caption wkuherald.com photograph library that names any of the 31 officers.

name: Lisa M. Kappler
fact: THE ONE STORY THAT IS ABOUT HER CARRIES NO PORTRAIT. The Herald of 17 February 2009 (84:22, p. 3) leads with 'SGA chief justice resigns', eight paragraphs on her resignation of 12 February 2009 with three quotations from her by e-mail, and it also quotes 'Vine Grove senior Corey Bewley, an associate justice on the judicial council'. The page was rendered and read: it carries no photograph of any person. Its only images are a Domino's Pizza advertisement, a Kentucky Tobacco Quit Line advertisement and a Great Escape Theatres advertisement, and the two mugshot-sized 188x278 images that a size heuristic flags are the Jonas Brothers and 'Fired Up!' film posters inside that last advertisement. Her name also appears in the text of 2 September 2004 (80:4, p. 3), 10 April 2008 (83:46, p. 5, the Judicial Council tie and campaign complaint story), 22 April 2008 (83:49, p. 6) and 12 February 2009 (84:21, p. 1); none of those pages photographs her either. Her two surviving wkuherald.com articles of February 2009, 'SGA Chief Justice Resigns' and 'SGA Sets Date For Student Regent Election', are archived with nothing but the masthead GIF and a print-edition thumbnail.

name: Corey Bewley
fact: QUOTED THROUGHOUT THE SPRING OF 2009 AND NEVER PHOTOGRAPHED. Every Herald page of 2008-09 whose text names him was cross-referenced against the print caption index and each page's photographs listed: 17 February (84:22, p. 3, the chief justice resignation story, rendered and read in full - no portrait on the page), 26 February (84:35, p. 1), 5 March (84:37, p. 3), 31 March (84:41, p. 6), 2 April (84:42, p. 3), 9 April (84:44, p. 6), 16 April (84:46, pp. 1 and 5) and 30 April (84:50, p. 3). Not one of those pages carries a photograph whose caption names him, and the two pages checked frame by frame carry no unattributed portrait either. His only appearance in the surviving wkuherald.com library is the article of 26 February 2009, 'Gilley Elected Student Regent', whose single photograph is captioned 'Pineville senior Reagan Gilley celebrates winning the Student Government Association student regent election'. The Herald printed his words and never his face.

name: VaShae Swope

The whole issue was searched: her name occurs on page 1 only, and the story's jump page carries no further mention. She is also named in the text of 7 April 2009 (84:43, p. 9), 16 April 2009 (84:46, p. 1) and 13 November 2009 (85:19, p. 3), none of which photographs her. name: SOURCE FOUND, NEVER RECORDED BEFORE - the 2013 and 2014 Talismans
fact: THE 2010s HAD MORE YEARBOOKS THAN THIS PROJECT THOUGHT. _archive-gaps.json states that the 2016 Talisman is 'the only Talisman of the 2010s with a complete portrait section' and the file contains no mention anywhere of a 2013 or a 2014 volume. Both exist and are digitised: UA12/2/2 2013 Talisman: Form, dlsc_ua_records/8696, article 9683; UA12/2/2 2014 Talisman: Reckoning Part I, dlsc_ua_records/5160, article 6164, 357,825,356 bytes; and Part II, dlsc_ua_records/5162, article 6167. Found by reading the dlsc_ua_yearbooks collection listing rather than by searching for a name. They cover the academic years 2012-13 and 2013-14 exactly, which is where nine of this block's officers sit. All three were pulled through the Wayback range route into ~/Desktop/SGA60 photo hunt/_topscholar-pdfs/ as talisman2013-form.pdf, talisman2014-reckoning-1.pdf and talisman2014-reckoning-2.pdf. Whatever this run concludes about them, the volumes are now on disk and no later run should treat the 2010s as having only 2015 and 2016.
